BUG (lifter.ts isRegister): tested 'regSize(s) > 0', but regSize() falls back to 4 for any unrecognised name, so the predicate was TRUE FOR EVERY STRING — every operand was treated as a register and immediates were lifted as registers. BUG (lifter.ts collectArgs32): walked backwards from the call and then called args.reverse(). Walking backwards ALREADY yields argument order — cdecl pushes right-to-left, so the push nearest the call is argument 1 — so the reverse() double-reversed and every reconstructed 32-bit call had its argument list backwards. Removed, with a comment explaining the ordering so it is not 're-fixed' back in.

ALSO FOUND (separate, serious — resource parser DoS): the MAX_DEPTH limit did not bound work. Each directory declares its own entry count in two uint16s, so one can claim 131070 children, and each child can point at a DISTINCT subdirectory offset that the 'visited' set cannot collapse. A 256 KB crafted .rsrc exhausted a 4 GB heap in under a minute — in a browser that is a dead tab, on a tool whose entire purpose is opening untrusted binaries. Fixed with a global MAX_TOTAL_ENTRIES budget (65536) threaded through the walk, surfaced as ResourceTree.truncated. Also clamped resource strings to 4096 chars: String.fromCharCode(...chars) with a 65535-element spread is at or over some engines' argument limit, and parseVersionInfo now keeps scanning for the terminator while capping collection so 'end' stays correct.

THE BUG: structureCFG built the general conditional as 'if (negate(condition)) { branchTarget } else { fallthrough }'. But condition is the condition under which the jcc is TAKEN, and branchTarget is the block reached when it IS taken. The guard was inverted while the bodies stayed in place. A 'je' on ecx == 0 emitted 'if (ecx != 0)' wrapped around the block that runs when ecx IS zero. Loop headers had the same inversion. Silent — the output was always plausible C describing the opposite of the binary.

I DID NOT TAKE THE AGENT'S WORD FOR THIS. It flipped 56 lines of existing assertions to match, which is the signature of papering over a wrong change, so the tests could not be evidence. Verified independently from x86 semantics:
1. getCondition('je') -> 'x == 0'; every entry in condMap is taken-polarity (jg->'>', jbe->'u<=', js->'< 0'). Uniform, no family-specific exception.
2. identifyBranches resolves branchTarget by matching the jcc operand address, so it does not depend on succs ordering.
3. No compensating negation downstream: cleanup.ts:66 is a paired swap-and-negate (polarity-agnostic), cfgpatterns.ts returns its own self-contained (condition, trueTarget, falseTarget) triple, emit.ts never negates.
4. DECISIVE: the short-circuit path in the SAME function already emitted 'if (scCond) { trueTarget } else { falseTarget }' un-negated. The two paths in one file contradicted each other.
5. RegState.negate's own docstring reads 'for structuring: if-not-taken path' — the codebase documents the correct rule and the code violated it.

DONE. Merging is now evidence-based wherever call-site provenance exists.

DESIGN. Two provenance maps kept deliberately apart:
- paramLinks: the struct a CALLER passed into funcAddr:paramIdx.
- paramViews: the struct the CALLEE itself built from that parameter.
A merge always requires the callee's corroboration, so two unrelated callers passing objects into the same slot are NOT linked to each other unless the callee actually dereferences that parameter as a struct. A passthrough helper taking a void* therefore links nothing. Identity is published in both directions, so caller-then-callee and callee-then-caller give the same answer — this REDUCES the order-dependence noted on peek-a-bin-z0r for the provenance path (the shape path's first-match-wins scan is unchanged).

THE CAPABILITY CAME BACK. A provenance-backed merge ignores MIN_SUBSET_MERGE_FIELDS, so the two-field partial view that z0r's guard had to give up now completes from a caller's fuller view — on evidence rather than shape coincidence. Pinned by 'completes a two-field parameter view from a struct the caller passed in'. Provenance still cannot override hasBoundaryConflict: contradictory layouts mean one reading is wrong.

DEFECT I FOUND AND FIXED IN THE AGENT'S WORK — this one mattered. It mapped stack parameters via /^arg_(\d+)$/ and used N as the argument index. But stack.ts:139 names them with a RUNNING COUNTER over the slots a function was OBSERVED to touch ('arg_${paramIdx}', paramIdx++ per entry), not by argument position. A 32-bit function that never reads its first argument names its SECOND argument arg_0. The caller side records the true index, so the two would link mismatched slots and merge unrelated structs — precisely the false merge this bead exists to eliminate. IRParam carries no offset so the true index is unrecoverable in structs.ts; I removed the stack-parameter path entirely and documented why. Provenance now reaches x64 register arguments only: fewer merges, none of them wrong. The agent's test for the removed path was replaced with one pinning the conservative behaviour.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH FILING: fix arg_N numbering in stack.ts, where the offset is still in hand, then stack-argument provenance becomes safe to enable. That would extend this to 32-bit binaries, which it currently does not cover at all.

FIXED. Commit 33f5ded. N is now derived from the slot offset instead of a counter over observed slots.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST is the gate, which goes beyond what I asked for and is the right call: numbering only happens for a VERIFIED frame-pointer prologue (push rbp / mov rbp, rsp, seeing through MSVC hot-patch padding). Under frame-pointer omission RBP is more often a callee-saved object pointer than a frame pointer, so [rbp+0x10] is frequently a STRUCT FIELD ACCESS rather than a parameter. Numbering those would have fed precisely the false struct merges this bead exists to prevent — it would have made provenance net harmful rather than useful. Slots in unverified frames are named by offset (arg_0x10), which the ^arg_(\d+)$ provenance pattern deliberately does not match. Since IRParam carries only name and type, the name is the only channel to structs.ts, so trust had to be encoded in it.

x64 SHADOW SPACE, which I asked to be checked because it is where an off-by-one would hide: the first slot [rbp+0x10] is the ABI home slot for the argument passed in RCX, not the first stack-only argument, so (offset - 0x10)/8 gives 0..3 for the home slots and 4 for the fifth argument at [rbp+0x30]. Confirmed intentional and pinned by 'numbers the fifth x64 argument past the shadow space'.

REGISTER vs STACK CONFLICT: I suggested preferring the register mapping; the agent chose the opposite and justified it, and it is right. RCX is volatile and routinely reused as scratch after being spilled to its home slot, so crediting later accesses through RCX to parameter 0 is the more dangerous reading. Pinned by 'gives a contested argument index to the stack slot, not the register'.

I ALSO CHECKED for the bug class I hit earlier this session (field_0x-8, an invalid C identifier from a negative offset): isParam is only recorded when offset >= minParamOffset, which equals firstOffset, so delta cannot be negative and arg_-1 is unreachable. Properly guarded.

IS IT DRIFT OR INTENT? Intent. The same files appear in both the upper- and lower-case lists (HexView 12 up / 2 low, Sidebar 6 / 2, InstructionDetail 3 / 2), which LOOKS like drift until you read what each formats. The variation is correlated with the KIND of value, consistently:
- ADDRESSES -> uppercase with 0x prefix. Consistent everywhere (Sidebar 206/372/444/466/614/668, InstructionDetail 232/277/296).
- RAW BYTES -> lowercase, padStart(2,'0'). Consistent (InstructionDetail 38-123, hex dump).
- SIZES AND OFFSETS -> lowercase, unpadded (section virtualSize, frame size).
- SEARCH AND COMPARISON -> .toLowerCase(), e.g. Sidebar:183 inside a match predicate. Deliberate normalisation, not display.

So a shared helper would need options for case, padding and prefix at nearly every call site, which buys essentially nothing over the inline call, and carries real risk: it touches ~195 sites across mostly components, and THERE IS NO REACT RENDERER here, so no test would catch a display regression.

THIS IS THE ONE ITEM ON peek-a-bin-brf.2 WHERE THE EVIDENCE POINTED THE OTHER WAY. Every other duplicate there had already diverged — parseBranchTarget's two copies behaved differently, nine rip parsers disagreed on case, two API lists were out of sync by seven entries, six modal copies had three tints and three Escape mechanisms. Deduplicating those was bug-removal. Here the variation is principled, so deduplicating would be churn.

WHAT THE SURVEY DID FIND, fixed in f4efa98: InstructionDetail:324 rendered '-0x{v.offset}' for EVERY stack frame entry. StackVar.offset is the operand value as written and is documented 'always positive'; the list holds locals below the frame pointer AND parameters above it. So a parameter at [rbp+0x10] displayed as -0x10, as did any [rsp+0x10] local. StackVar now carries a signed signedOffset — the value already existed in stack.ts, folded into the key string and then thrown away — and the panel renders the sign from it. Same negative-number class as the field_0x-8 invalid-identifier bug fixed earlier this session.

That is the whole value of having surveyed rather than deduplicated: the sweep was worth doing, the refactor was not.

DONE. Commit 6519afa. All three items, and the Escape one was decided rather than applied.

ESCAPE — per dialog, via a pure predicate accidentalDismissAllowed({inFlight, unsavedWork}), not uniformly. A dialog streaming an LLM response or holding a table of pending rename decisions is closer to Settings than to a command palette: dismissing it by accident discards work. So the AI report becomes dismissible once its stream finishes but not while running, and batch rename's progress state is not dismissible at all. Settings keeps its deliberate non-dismissibility and its 'do not unify this' comment, untouched.

BODY SCROLL LOCK — a depth counter, not a boolean, so with two dialogs open the inner one closing does not unlock the page. It saves the INLINE body styles and restores exactly those rather than clearing overflow blindly and destroying whatever the page had set. paddingRight: null means 'leave it alone' and is deliberately distinct from '', which would clear an inline padding the page set for its own reasons. The scrollbar gutter is added back as padding so hiding the scrollbar does not widen the viewport and shift the page sideways. All three of those are the classic ways a scroll lock goes wrong and all three are handled.

ARIA-LABELLEDBY — naming is now a discriminated union: either label or labelledBy, never both and never neither. That is a type-level guarantee no dialog can be unnamed, which is stronger than the convention it replaces. Pointing at a visible heading is preferred because the accessible name then matches what a sighted user reads.

The lock arithmetic and naming rules are pure functions in modalScaffold.ts taking measurements as parameters, so they are tested without a DOM — same reason the focus arithmetic was split out there.
